sources.title: Repository tagged hand-written HashMap interview question
Independent SimpleHashMap structure and differential validation

claims.text: The preserved source requires an array-plus-linked-list HashMap with basic put/get and does not specify full JDK behavior, resizing, deletion, null or concurrency semantics.
The exact candidate uses a bucket array with linked collision nodes; distinct same-hash keys coexist and equal keys overwrite under the declared contract.
Bucket indexing remains legal for negative/extreme hashes and lookup/update behavior matches the reference Map across forced and randomized tests under the non-null contract.

For b buckets, n entries and target-chain length L, the implementation performs O(1+L) bucket-plus-chain work, degrades to O(n) for a single long chain, uses O(b+n) storage, and intentionally omits resize/concurrency semantics.

validation.command: extract exact candidate Java; javac -Xlint:all -Werror; reflect structure; forced collision/overwrite/hash-boundary tests; 24000 seeded differential operations vs java.util.HashMap under declared contract

checks: exact candidate Java compiles with warnings as errors
bucket field is an array and node contains same-type next link
200 forced same-hash keys coexist and a middle key overwrites correctly
24000 seeded put/get operations across six capacities match reference HashMap under non-null contract
zero/negative capacity and null key/value boundaries reject

boundary_tests.case: duplicate equal key after long collision chain
boundary_tests.expected: existing value overwritten without breaking other keys
all indexes remain legal and values retrievable
null key/value operations reject and missing get returns null

findings: The preserved repository source requires only a hand-written HashMap with an array, linked-list collision structure, and basic put/get behavior; it does not require full JDK HashMap compatibility, resizing, deletion, iteration, treeification, null support, or concurrency.

The candidate preserves that sparse boundary and clearly labels fixed capacity, non-null keys/values, overwrite-on-duplicate, missing-get returns null, no resize, and no thread-safety as answer-side contracts rather than source facts.

The implementation has the required structure: a bucket array whose component node has a same-type next link, so collisions are represented by separate chaining rather than by an unbounded flat scan or collision overwrite.

Bucket selection and identity are correctly separated: the mixed hash plus Math.floorMod chooses a legal bucket even for negative/extreme hashes, while equals decides key identity inside the chain, allowing distinct same-hash keys to coexist.

put updates an existing equal key before inserting a new head node, and get traverses the same bucket chain; reviewer-owned validation covers a 200-node forced collision chain, overwrite of a middle key, and missing-key behavior.

The remediated answer now states both time and space bounds required by the Coding standard: O(1+L) per operation for target-chain length L, O(n) worst case, and O(b+n) storage for b buckets and n entries.

Reviewer-owned differential validation runs 24,000 seeded operations across six capacities against java.util.HashMap under the candidate declared non-null/fixed-capacity contract, plus explicit Integer.MIN_VALUE/-1/0/MAX_VALUE hash cases and constructor/null boundaries.

No fabricated production experience, placeholder implementation, uncovered source variant, or unsupported JDK-version threshold is asserted; expansion topics are kept as follow-up boundaries rather than silently changing the requested minimal implementation.
